organizations.canonical_name: United States Office of Price Administration
organizations.normalization_notes: The historical wartime agency is retained separately from the later Office of Price Stabilization. An undated or later General Counsel reference is not used as a pre-OSS role.
The federal department is normalized without inferring an undocumented bureau or office for individual affiliations.

affiliations.date_precision: after Harvard Law School graduation in 1938 and before wartime Army and OSS service; exact dates not established
affiliations.research_notes: The American Law Institute chronology places Office of Price Administration staff work after Auerbach's 1938 law degree and before wartime overseas OSS service. This is the best-supported last civilian affiliation before military service, but it is not labeled immediate pre-OSS because the intervening Army chronology and exact OSS entry date remain unresolved.

affiliations.date_precision: after a two-month law-firm position following 1938 graduation; before Office of Price Administration and wartime service
affiliations.research_notes: The University of Minnesota Law School chronology explicitly places a Department of Labor position after a brief law-firm job following Auerbach's 1938 graduation. Because later Office of Price Administration work is documented, Labor is published only as an earlier prewar government affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Second Lieutenant Carl A. Auerbach is strongly matched to lawyer Carl Auerbach, who served in the Army and with the OSS in London.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War II he was drafted into the Army and served with the Office of Strategic Services in London
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two institutional memorials identify Carl Auerbach as an Army serviceman assigned to the OSS, including overseas service in London.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the exact uncommon name, Army service, officer-compatible wartime chronology, and explicit OSS service align with the visually verified Second Lieutenant index row. The private identifier has not yet been checked against a personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish wartime Army and OSS service but do not provide the exact induction, commission, transfer, or OSS entry dates.
claims.match_notes: Born in Brooklyn in 1915 and graduated from Harvard Law School in 1938. Box 26 remains necessary for direct identifier confirmation and precise wartime sequence.

claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last documented civilian government affiliation in the available chronology. It is not called immediate pre-OSS because an Army interval is documented and its assignment sequence is unknown.
